propositions.name: Units of hbar
propositions.statement: The reduced Planck constant has the units of action: \([\hbar] = \mathrm{J\,s}\).

propositions.name: Time in natural units
propositions.statement: In natural units with energy in eV, time has the dimension of inverse energy, \([t] = \mathrm{eV^{-1}}\).

propositions.name: Length in natural units
propositions.statement: In natural units with energy in eV, length has the dimension of inverse energy, \([L] = \mathrm{eV^{-1}}\).

propositions.name: Rest energy
propositions.statement: A particle of mass \(m\) at rest has rest energy \(E_0 = mc^2\).

propositions.name: Total energy
propositions.statement: The total energy of a particle of mass \(m\) moving with Lorentz factor \(\gamma\) is \(E = \gamma m c^2\).

propositions.name: de Broglie relation
propositions.statement: A particle with momentum \(p\) has de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = h/p\).

propositions.name: hbar c
propositions.statement: The conversion constant \(\hbar c \approx 197\ \mathrm{MeV\,fm}\) is used for nuclear-scale calculations.

propositions.name: Non-relativistic kinetic energy
propositions.statement: The kinetic energy \(T = E - mc^2\) reduces to \(T \approx p^2/2m\) only when \(pc \ll mc^2\).

propositions.name: Natural units
propositions.statement: In natural units \(\hbar = c = 1\) and every quantity is measured in powers of energy.

arguments.message:
## Units of \(\hbar\) and natural units

The reduced Planck constant \(\hbar = h/2\pi\) has the units of action: \([\hbar] = \mathrm{J\,s}\), the same as angular momentum. In particle physics we usually quote \(\hbar\) in \(\mathrm{eV\,s}\).

In **natural units** we set \(\hbar = c = 1\) and measure everything in powers of energy, with energy in eV. Then \(E = \hbar\omega\) means a frequency has the dimension of energy, and time has the dimension of inverse energy: \([t] = [E]^{-1} = \mathrm{eV^{-1}}\). Length is also an inverse energy, \([L] = \mathrm{eV^{-1}}\).

A particle of mass \(m\) at rest has rest energy \(E_0 = mc^2\). For the rest of the course we keep \(E_0\) for rest energy and \(E\) for total energy, \(E = \gamma m c^2\).

The de Broglie relation \(\lambda = h/p\) gives the wavelength of a particle with momentum \(p\). A useful number for nuclear scales is \(\hbar c \approx 197\ \mathrm{MeV\,fm}\); you will calculate with it all the time.

The kinetic energy is \(T = E - mc^2\). It reduces to \(T \approx p^2/2m\) only when the particle is non-relativistic, \(pc \ll mc^2\).

Nuclear sizes are a few femtometres: the prefix femto- (f) means \(10^{-15}\).
